chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) broke his fast on a Thursday evening in Masjid Quba. He asked, 'Is there any drink?' So Aws ibn Khawla al-Ansari brought him a cup of buttermilk mixed with honey. When he placed it on his lips, he set it aside and then said: 'Two drinks, yet one would suffice for the other. I will not drink it, nor do I forbid it, but I humble myself before Allah. Indeed, whoever humbles himself before Allah, Allah elevates him; and whoever is arrogant, Allah abases him. Whoever is moderate in his livelihood, Allah grants him sustenance; and whoever is wasteful, Allah deprives him. And whoever remembers Allah often, Allah loves him.'

key_terms.عَسٍ: A cup or vessel for drinking
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ قُبَاءٍ: Masjid Quba, the first mosque in Islam

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet setting aside his drink of buttermilk and honey?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Prophet’s voluntary abstinence (*zuhd*) rather than obligatory prohibition, illustrating the Shia emphasis on conscious spiritual choice. The incident at Masjid Quba serves as a practical lesson in *tawadu* (humility), linking the physical act of setting aside the drink to the metaphysical principle that God elevates the humble. It further connects ethical conduct in daily life—specifically moderation in sustenance and remembrance of God—to divine favor and love.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 1.Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, “Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj who said, ‘I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say, “

The Messenger of Allah opened his fast on a Thursday night at Masjid Qubā. He asked, ‘Is there anything to drink?’ So Aws ibn Khawlah al-Anṣārī brought him a cup of buttermilk [mixed] with honey. When he placed it on his lips [and took a sip], he set it aside and then said, ‘Two drinks [in one] while any of them would suffice on its own. I will not drink it, but I do not forbid it. Rather, I humble myself before Allah, for indeed whoever humbles himself before Allah is elevated by Allah, and whoever is arrogant is abased by Allah. Whoever is moderate in his lifestyle is granted [an increase in] sustenance by Allah, but whoever is wasteful [and extravagant] is deprived by Allah. And whoever remembers Allah often is loved by Allah.’”
